affected_system: municipal capital planning, debt, grants, reserves, procurement, and asset delivery
alternatives: verify the highest-consequence signals before acting on capital obligation, backlog, and delivery risk
combine targeted inspection, monitoring, and data-quality repair for capital obligation, backlog, and delivery risk
pair asset-budget-contract-schedule reconciliation with an explicit stop, review, and escalation rule
assumptions: Budgets, obligations, appropriations, encumbrances, expenditures, schedules, and assets are reconciled.
All fiscal scenarios separate nominal, real, committed, contingent, and modeled amounts.
All alternatives, capacities, costs, effects, thresholds, and failure scenarios are proposed until bound to evidence.
baseline: continue current inspection and reporting practice for capital obligation, backlog, and delivery risk.

constraints.description: The capital portfolio and municipal finance diagnose must respect declared measurement resolution and classification uncertainty.
Every released metric must retain evidence type, source lineage, geography, time, assumptions, and uncertainty.
No analytical output may bypass lawful authority, accountable human review, or an applicable appeal process.

decision_cadence: recompiled at each planning cycle and after material evidence change
decision_owner: chief financial officer and capital planning director
decision_question: Which assets and projects show reconciled condition need, cost growth, delay, funding gap, or delivery risk?

independence_key.binding_constraint: The capital portfolio and municipal finance diagnose must respect declared measurement resolution and classification uncertainty.
independence_key.decision_object: capital obligation, backlog, and delivery risk
independence_key.evidence_gate: Evidence for capital obligation, backlog, and delivery risk passes documented checks for coverage, semantics, geography, timestamps, and uncertainty.
independence_key.primary_outcome: verified high-consequence unfunded or delayed obligations

intended_claim: A versioned diagnose design for comparing declared alternatives affecting capital obligation, backlog, and delivery risk, conditional on its evidence gate.
limitations: This library record has no city binding and therefore reports no local input, output, or recommendation.
Readiness describes explicit source and method gates; it does not certify implementation feasibility.
External domain, legal, community, security, and operational review remains outside this design artifact.

objectives.metric: verified high-consequence unfunded or delayed obligations
distributional gap in verified high-consequence unfunded or delayed obligations
decision claims with complete evidence lineage

prohibited_claims: Do not call a request, estimate, or plan an audited liability, appropriation, or expenditure.
Do not describe a design-only record as a city execution, deployment, adopted policy, or impact result.
Do not relabel proposed, estimated, simulated, optimized, or causal evidence as observed evidence.
Do not infer individual behavior, protected status, harm, or entitlement from aggregate records.

release_gate.failure_release: Release an explicit insufficient-evidence record naming missing sources, failed diagnostics, prohibited claims, and the next validation action.
release_gate.pass_condition: Evidence for capital obligation, backlog, and delivery risk passes documented checks for coverage, semantics, geography, timestamps, and uncertainty.

title: Diagnose capital obligations, backlog, and delivery friction
transportability_risks: Accounting, tax authority, debt limits, grants, procurement, labor, and markets differ.
Historical delivery and cost relationships may shift under inflation or policy change.
